answer: Harness-attestation fingerprinting hashes each agent's runtime manifest into a jade fingerprint, binds it to a rotating zephyr challenge, and folds cross-agent matches into a time-decayed tide score. Admission costs a per-identity bond, a fixed fee per attestation attempt, a five-peer quorum, and a 72-hour trust ramp under a one-identity-per-hour cap. A coordinated ring fails because shared harness fingerprints make its attestations cluster, so peers correlate the whole set, refuse quorum, and slash the bonds.
